## Remediation complete — change 2982, evidence

Commit `c821b03ea65` on `fix-2d65-autodeploy`, based on `ddb1d953812`. Files:
`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`, and a new
`tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_self_update_reexec.py` (444 insertions, 12 deletions).
`rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev HEAD` → `OK - resolved 2d65-32dd-28b9-43ef`.

### Root cause, confirmed in the current file

The mcp roll runs `rsync "$MIRROR_DIR/" "$DEPLOY_REPO/"` — which on the box overwrites the
running script — and *then* calls `mcp_run_new`. bash executes the body it already parsed,
so the container is built from the previous body. Two adjacent defects were confirmed the
same way: `autodeploy.sh` was absent from `MCP_PATHS` (a body-only change fires no roll at
all), and the up-to-date early exit returned before component deltas were computed, so
resetting only `mcp-deployed-sha` was a permanent no-op. That matches the operator finding
that only resetting **both** markers recovered.

### AC1 — reproduced; test fails before the fix

```
python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_self_update_reexec.py::test_body_change_reaches_the_container_built_in_the_same_tick -p no:randomly -q
```

```
E       AssertionError: the container was built from the STALE mcp_run_new body — the new
        flag is absent from the constructed `docker run` argv
E         rc=2
E         'run --name rebar-mcp-eeeeeeeeeeee-8092 -p 8092 :: run -d --name
          rebar-mcp-eeeeeeeeeeee-8092 --restart always --label rebar.service=mcp
          --memory 3712m ... -v /var/lib/rebar:/var/lib/rebar compose-mcp:eeee…'
E         STDERR=…/deploy/infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh: line 965: unexpected EOF while
          looking for matching `"'
E       assert 'REBAR_BODY_MARKER=applied' in 'run --name rebar-mcp-eeeeeeeeeeee-8092 …'
FAILED tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_self_update_reexec.py::test_body_change_reaches_the_container_built_in_the_same_tick
1 failed in 3.52s
```

All four new tests fail against pre-fix code.

### AC2 — the changed body reaches the created container

```
.                                                                        [100%]
1 passed
```

```
rc= 0
run_line_count= 1
mcp-deployed-sha= eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
MARKER_PRESENT= True
ARGV_SNIPPET: ... eee-8092 --restart always --label rebar.service=mcp -e REBAR_BODY_MARKER=applied --me ...
```

### AC3–AC4 — no loop, and markers cannot claim an unapplied body

```
tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_self_update_reexec.py::test_body_change_reaches_the_container_built_in_the_same_tick PASSED [ 25%]
tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_self_update_reexec.py::test_consecutive_ticks_roll_exactly_once_no_loop PASSED [ 50%]
tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_self_update_reexec.py::test_marker_state_matches_the_container_that_was_built PASSED [ 75%]
tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_self_update_reexec.py::test_component_marker_behind_global_current_still_rolls PASSED [100%]
============================== 4 passed in 15.25s ==============================
```

Existing autodeploy suite: 80 passed, no regression.

### AC5 — runbook corrected

The prior note ("a commit touching *only* `autodeploy.sh` triggers no deploy — hand-deploy
it") was wrong post-fix and was corrected rather than appended to. The new section records
the symptom, the ordering that causes it, and the recovery requiring **both** markers reset.

### AC6 — lint and typecheck

`make lint` → 0. `make typecheck` → 0 (`Success: no issues found in 771 source files`).
Complexity ratchet: `active=32 new=0 increased=0 stale=17`. Mechanism ratchet: exit 0 — the
new shell variable `AUTODEPLOY_REEXEC_GEN` is not a counted mechanism (the detector scans
only `src/rebar` for `REBAR_*`), so no marker was added.

### Design: re-exec after each source-sync rsync

A snapshot of `SELF_PATH` is taken under the existing single-flight `flock`;
`reexec_if_self_changed` compares it to the installed file and, on a difference, re-execs
once. Loop-freedom: after the re-exec the installed body equals the fresh process's own
snapshot (the mirror sync is idempotent, TARGET pinned), so the comparison matches and it
does not re-exec; a `max=2` generation cap carried across `exec` is a hard stop.
`MCP_PATHS` now includes `autodeploy.sh`, and the early exit requires component markers to
equal TARGET — those two must move together, as this ticket warned.

**Rejected:** making the component delta consider the script's own content (the same-tick
roll still runs the stale body, then stamps the marker — requiring exactly the loop-prone
"skip stamping, roll again" logic the ACs forbid); and splitting install from roll across
two ticks (adds a phase-marker mechanism and delays every deploy by a full tick).

Kept in bash deliberately: the defect *is* a shell-runtime property — a running bash process
serving a body its file no longer contains. Migrating to Python would have tested a
reimplementation rather than the artifact that fails in production. The test runs the real
script as a subprocess and asserts on the constructed `docker run` argv, with no Docker
daemon and no CI-provider dependency.

### `make verify`: red, and 2d65 is not the cause

33 failures. All 33 reproduce on a worktree at the same base **without** this change:

| Class | Count | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| pandoc (`test_wiki_render` 13, `test_rich_text_cutover` 3, `test_diff_comments_cutover_neutral` 1) | 17 | `dc28` / `9119` |
| doctor (`test_doctor_dirty_tree` 5, `test_doctor` 5) | 10 | `8c5f` |
| sandbox/SemLock (`marker_fcntl`, `doctor_locks`, `atomic_completion_close`, `completion_gate`, `network_guard_local_ipc`, `sandbox_capabilities_985f`) | 6 | `0eba` / `985f` |

None is an autodeploy test, and none touches a file this change modifies. The earlier
"16 residual" figure reconciles exactly: that measurement ran in a worktree with
`PYPANDOC_PANDOC` set, which removes precisely the 17 pandoc failures. 33 − 17 = 16.

### Adjacent finding, characterized only

When the rsync replaces the running script with a file of *different length*, bash's lazy
block-buffered read of its own script desyncs and the interpreter can die mid-tick with
`unexpected EOF while looking for matching "` (observed at line 965), leaving markers
partially stamped and a component half-rolled. The re-exec fix eliminates this face too, so
no separate work is required.
